searchText: What would have happened if the bug in the code was on geth? How come 3 testnets didnt find it? Great job for the quick solution! Can anyone here help me understand why this transaction is failing? https://etherscan.io/tx/0xf367a95315d61f484306ca7e97f963bbf1ed181b86aa7932c92db72542917cce It is trying to send some ETH to a forwarder contract which just does this on ETH receipt: ``` parentAddress.call.value(msg.value)(msg.data) ``` Looking at the VM Trace/Geth Trace/Parity Trace, the `CALL` opcode is using 12,687 gas according to vmTrace and `10187` gas according to Geth trace (`msg.data` is empty bytes), and also weird is that the callee is only receiving 3387 gas (even though there was way more than that available at the call site. Hmm, maybe an issue with the version of Solidity that built it... IIUC, it is pushing a hard-coded value onto the stack and subtracting that from the remaining gas and then passing the result to `CALL` for the `gas` parameter I believe. Essentially, it seems to be trying to "reserve" some gas for after the call. And for reasons I don't fully understand, the amount of gas it is trying to reserve is pretty large (~35000). Hey this is really off-topic but I'm not working at SigmaPrime anymore, so feel free to remove my `SigP` tag ^^' <@552133098075193354> I think has the power? ☝️ I may be a little daft with this, but could somebody please explain this block to me please? https://etherchain.org/block/12251109 How is there a 69 eth MEV reward? https://etherscan.io/tx/0x284389466e78ac3f76efaefc83824aeae13ddf729ef1383e062e33c004a90a36#statechange That transaction has 69.69 ETH sent to the block miner. I get that. But more wondering how one specified miner tip/mev? Is it all done in the transaction/swop or how does it come out with 69 eth worth of mev extraction? Someone sent 69 ETH to block.coinbase in their transaction. spam 🤡 Spam ^2 <@!832552088390205462> spamming We may need a #spam channel. does discord do anything about these spammers? if not, this will be endless Able Tie#4048 We don't like the idea of adding restrictions on who can join the server, or capcha stuff via DM etc. like some other servers do. As long as there's no spam in the server I think we just keep things as-is, and deal with the occasional spam in DMs :(. Discord has this option. It doesn't prevent bots. But maybe in the future we can add a simple entry-question (e.g. what is the name of the next eth1 hardfork) to filter out bots. We can give it a try though Will discuss with mods FWIW I think as of now dealing with the small amount of spam isn't as bad as potentially turning away a potential contributor. Not a very strong opinion though. answering a simple enough question is a pretty low bar We introduced this. If not accepting, bots can't DM others in the server. Hope that's strong enough. There's a small greyed-out option (in settings panel) to ask a short question to new users, Discord is working on the feature we need.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content:
Can anyone here help me understand why this transaction is failing?
https://etherscan.io/tx/0xf367a95315d61f484306ca7e97f963bbf1ed181b86aa7932c92db72542917cce
It is trying to send some ETH to a forwarder contract which just does this on ETH receipt:
```
parentAddress.call.value(msg.value)(msg.data)
```
Looking at the VM Trace/Geth Trace/Parity Trace, the `CALL` opcode is using 12,687 gas according to vmTrace and `10187` gas according to Geth trace (`msg.data` is empty bytes), and also weird is that the callee is only receiving 3387 gas (even though there was way more than that available at the call site.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Hmm, maybe an issue with the version of Solidity that built it... IIUC, it is pushing a hard-coded value onto the stack and subtracting that from the remaining gas and then passing the result to `CALL` for the `gas` parameter I believe.  Essentially, it seems to be trying to "reserve" some gas for after the call.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: And for reasons I don't fully understand, the amount of gas it is trying to reserve is pretty large (~35000).
